title: test_channel_plan.py: EUI64 value 0 mishandled due to falsy or evaluation
description: Line 210: `eui_hex = inp.get("eui64") or inp.get("eui64_hex", "")` uses `or` which treats integer 0 as falsy. If a test vector has `"eui64": 0` (all-zeros EUI64), the code falls through to `eui64_hex` or empty string. `bytes.fromhex("")` produces `b""` instead of 8 zero bytes. The hash is then computed over 4 bytes (epoch only) instead of 12 bytes (8 EUI + 4 epoch), producing wrong results. Fix: use `inp.get("eui64") if "eui64" in inp else inp.get("eui64_hex", "")`.
close_reason: Issue already fixed: the problematic pattern (inp.get("eui64") or inp.get("eui64_hex", "")) does not exist in test_channel_plan.py. Current code uses safe direct indexing with explicit key assertions. All 33 tests pass.
